heroText: Helsinki is Finland's sea-facing capital, built around design, ferries, saunas and easy public transport. Start at Helsinki Cathedral and Market Square, take the ferry to Suomenlinna, then use the Design District or Oodi Library for a modern city day. Helsinki Airport connects smoothly by train to the centre.

areas.name: Kluuvi
areas.text: Kluuvi is the central station and shopping core, best for first stays, rail arrivals and short walks to landmarks.

areas.name: Kamppi
areas.text: Kamppi has hotels, malls, restaurants and transport links, making it practical for short urban stays.

areas.name: Punavuori
areas.text: Punavuori anchors the Design District with cafes, boutiques and a more local evening feel.

areas.name: Katajanokka
areas.text: Katajanokka is a quieter harbour district near ferries, Art Nouveau streets and Market Square.

airports.name: Helsinki Airport (HEL)
airports.text: Helsinki Airport is north of the city and links to central Helsinki by frequent commuter trains and buses.

airportTransfer.value: 30-35 min by train to Helsinki Central Station
airportTransfer.distance: about 18 km north of the centre

stayOverview: Choose Kluuvi for the central station and classic first walks, Kamppi for transport and restaurants, Punavuori for design-led local evenings, or Katajanokka for harbour atmosphere and quieter streets.
hotelIntro: Helsinki is easy by tram, metro and train. Central hotels are convenient, but Punavuori and Katajanokka often give more neighbourhood character while staying close to major sights and ferry routes.
rentalCars: Do not rent for Helsinki; trains, trams and ferries work better unless leaving for rural Finland.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Stay in Kluuvi or Kamppi for a first short visit, especially if arriving by train from the airport.

travelTips.title: Ferries
travelTips.text: Suomenlinna ferries run from Market Square, but weather and ice can affect the feel of the trip.

travelTips.title: Sauna
travelTips.text: For sauna time in Helsinki, confirm booking rules, swim access and the route back to your hotel before committing.

travelTips.title: Day trip
travelTips.text: Porvoo is the classic old-town day trip, with wooden houses and riverside cafes east of Helsinki.

After the Russians captured Helsinki in May 1713 during the Great Northern War, the retreating Swedish administration set fire to parts of the city.
The Russians besieged the Sveaborg fortress during the war, and about a quarter of the city was destroyed in a fire in 1808.
Emperor Alexander I of Russia moved the capital of Finland from Turku to Helsinki on 8 April 1812 to reduce Swedish influence in Finland and bring the capital closer to St Petersburg.
Official Finnish government documents and Finnish language newspapers have used the name Helsinki since 1819, when the Senate of Finland moved to the city from Turku, the former capital of Finland.
